evals.name: first-pass SHIP straight through the stages
evals.prompt: /grill-to-tickets Add a "copy shareable link" button to the report detail page that copies the report's existing public URL to the clipboard and shows a confirmation toast. One component, no API or schema change, acceptance behavior is explicit, and no open decisions remain — treat the Stage 0 frontier as empty and already confirmed.
evals.expected_output: With the Stage 0 frontier already empty and confirmed, pass straight through: synthesize spec.md with to-spec (Stage 1), run scrutinize once (Stage 2), normalize its closing line to SHIP, and advance to Stage 3 to-tickets. Publish tickets under .scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/ and print the /clear then /implement handoff.
expectations: Confirms the empty Stage 0 frontier, then moves through Stage 1 -> Stage 2 -> Stage 3 in order
Runs scrutinize exactly once and records cycle 1 with verdict SHIP in a single .scratch/<feature-slug>/design-review.md file
Normalizes the scrutinize verdict to the token SHIP with no paraphrasing
Does not enter FIX_THEN_SHIP, REWORK, or a backward transition to Stage 0
Prints the /clear then /implement <first ticket> handoff and never invokes the implement skill or spawns a stage subagent

evals.name: FIX_THEN_SHIP corrects a violated invariant in place
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue subtitle-preferences. Stage 2 scrutinize closes with fix-then-ship: the spec says the font-size preference is written to localStorage, but the Stage 0 ADR settled that per-device preferences live in the existing PreferencesStore. The design is right; one named store is wrong.
evals.expected_output: Normalize to FIX_THEN_SHIP. Name the violated invariant (the Stage 0 ADR), verify it, and make the smallest correct edit directly to spec.md — swap the named store. Consume one gate cycle, re-run scrutinize, and keep control in Stage 2.
expectations: Normalizes the verdict to the token FIX_THEN_SHIP
Edits .scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md in place as the minimal correction to the violated invariant
Consumes exactly one gate cycle and re-reviews within Stage 2
Does not re-run to-spec, return to Stage 0, or add a dependency the finding did not require

evals.name: spec-level REWORK re-runs to-spec inside the gate
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue wishlist-sync. This is gate cycle 2. Stage 2 scrutinize closes with rework: the empty-state behavior was settled in Stage 0, but the spec never wrote it as a user story and the persistence seam is stated too vaguely to break into tickets. Every fact needed to fix it is already in the Stage 0 transcript.
evals.expected_output: Diagnose spec-level REWORK — a fresh writer holding the Stage 0 transcript could fix the spec with no new decision. Re-run to-spec inline with the finding as added context, consume one gate cycle, and re-review. Control stays in Stage 2 and the cycle counter is not reset.
expectations: Records reworkKind: spec-level with reasoning that names the finding
Re-runs to-spec inline rather than returning to Stage 0
Consumes one gate cycle and re-reviews without leaving Stage 2
Does not reset the cycle counter, and keeps one stable design-review.md updated in place

evals.name: decision-level REWORK returns to Stage 0 without resetting the counter
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue wishlist-sync. This is gate cycle 3. Stage 2 scrutinize closes with rework: the spec assumes wishlists are private to one account, but a shared-household actor has surfaced that nobody decided on. to-spec cannot synthesize a decision that was never made.
evals.expected_output: Diagnose decision-level REWORK — the finding traces to a decision no one has made. Return to Stage 0, re-grill only that decision (inline grilling + domain-modeling), update CONTEXT.md and adr/, then re-run to-spec and re-review. The cycle counter carries the backward transition and stays at 3.
expectations: Records reworkKind: decision-level with reasoning that it traces to an unmade decision
Returns to Stage 0 and re-grills the specific decision, updating CONTEXT.md and adr/
Carries the cycle counter over the transition to Stage 0 and never resets it to 0 or 1
States which REWORK kind was diagnosed and why, so spec-level and decision-level are distinguished in the gate report

evals.name: REJECT halts and reports without auto-resuming grilling
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue offline-sync. Stage 2 scrutinize closes with reject: the core concept — full bidirectional offline sync with no conflict model — is unviable as scoped.
evals.expected_output: Normalize to REJECT, stop the gate immediately, and report to the user with the single biggest reason from scrutinize. A fresh attempt is a human decision, not an automatic transition.
expectations: Normalizes the verdict to the token REJECT and halts immediately
Reports to the user with the single biggest reason from scrutinize
Does not auto-resume Stage 0 grilling or open another gate cycle
Does not advance to Stage 3 ticket breakdown

evals.name: stall stops early before the budget is spent
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue payments-ledger. Gate cycles 2 and 3 both return the same single blocking finding — the reconciliation window is undefined — with no new and no resolved findings between them.
evals.expected_output: Detect the stall — the same blocking finding survived two consecutive cycles with no new and no resolved findings — and stop before cycle 6. Report the stalled finding, the spec fingerprints reviewed, and why no progress is possible.
expectations: Stops before the six-cycle gate budget is exhausted
Reports the repeated blocking finding and the spec fingerprints reviewed each cycle
Explains why no progress is possible rather than looping mechanically
Does not advance to Stage 3

evals.name: budget exhaustion at cycle 6 requires human authorization
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue payments-ledger. Gate cycle 6 has just completed and the verdict is still not SHIP — a mix of FIX_THEN_SHIP and REWORK across the six cycles, with findings still open.
evals.expected_output: Stop at 6/6. Report budget exhaustion with the unresolved findings and the per-cycle history, and state that a fresh six-cycle budget needs explicit human authorization and a materially different approach.
expectations: Records six completed cycles and never starts cycle 7 automatically
Reports budget exhaustion with the unresolved findings and the per-cycle history
States that a fresh budget requires explicit human authorization
Does not advance to Stage 3 ticket breakdown without a SHIP verdict

evals.name: reuse survey bootstraps a missing catalog with a pointer line
evals.prompt: /grill-to-tickets Add CSV export to the orders list page. The project has no docs/reuse-catalog.md yet; an AGENTS.md exists at the repository root.
evals.expected_output: In Stage 0, after grounding, run the Reuse survey: with no catalog, survey the areas the idea touches (the orders feature and the shared-code locations) through a read-only fact-lookup subagent, create docs/reuse-catalog.md from the template filled with entries for existing reusable modules and a Coverage line dated today per surveyed area, add one pointer line to AGENTS.md, and list these catalog changes in the Stage 0 pause summary.
expectations: Runs the Reuse survey in Stage 0 before the first grilling round
Creates docs/reuse-catalog.md from the template, with entries only for code that exists
Writes a Coverage line dated today for every surveyed area
Adds exactly one pointer line to AGENTS.md
Lists the catalog changes in the Stage 0 pause summary

evals.name: reuse survey drift check removes a stale entry
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets Add a refund button to the order detail page. docs/reuse-catalog.md lists `formatMoney` — `src/lib/money.ts`, but that file now exports only `formatCurrency`, and nothing in the repository defines formatMoney any more. src/lib/ is in Coverage, and money.ts changed after its Coverage date.
evals.expected_output: The drift check greps formatMoney in src/lib/money.ts, finds it absent there and anywhere else in the repository, and removes the entry. Because money.ts changed since the src/lib/ Coverage date, the gap survey re-reads it, adds an entry for formatCurrency, and moves the src/lib/ Coverage date to today. The Stage 0 summary reports the removal and the addition.
expectations: Removes the formatMoney entry after confirming the symbol is gone from the repository
Re-reads money.ts because it changed after the Coverage date, and adds a formatCurrency entry
Moves the src/lib/ Coverage date to today
Reports both catalog changes in the Stage 0 summary

evals.name: reuse survey re-reads only files changed in a covered area
evals.prompt: /grill-to-tickets Add a date-range filter to the reports page. docs/reuse-catalog.md has Coverage `src/features/reports/` — surveyed 2026-09-01, and since then only src/features/reports/use-report-query.ts has changed in that area. src/components/filters/ is not in Coverage.
evals.expected_output: Decide the gaps: for the covered src/features/reports/, re-read only use-report-query.ts (the one file the Coverage git log returns); survey all of the uncovered src/components/filters/. Leave the unchanged covered files unread. Write back entries for what was found and set both areas' Coverage dates to today.
expectations: Uses the Coverage date to limit src/features/reports/ to the changed file
Surveys the whole of the uncovered src/components/filters/
Leaves covered, unchanged files unread
Sets the Coverage date of both surveyed areas to today

evals.name: extend-vs-new reuse choice becomes a grilling question
evals.prompt: /grill-to-tickets Add row selection with bulk delete to the users table. docs/reuse-catalog.md lists `DataTable` — `src/components/ui/data-table.tsx` — use for: sortable, paginated tables. DataTable has no selection support today.
evals.expected_output: The survey establishes the fact (DataTable exists, lacks selection). Whether to extend DataTable with selection or build a separate selectable table is a real choice, so it joins the grilling frontier as a numbered question with a recommended answer (extend DataTable, keeping existing callers unchanged) and waits for the user's decision.
expectations: Treats DataTable's existence and lack of selection as facts, not questions
Asks extend-versus-new as a numbered frontier question with a recommended answer
Waits for the user's answer instead of deciding the reuse choice itself
